query:
The group settled on a formal protocol for logging parking incidents and a five-incidents-per-month escalation threshold. One member's response in that moment was distinctly different from the others'. Whose reaction signalled less than full agreement, and what specifically in how they responded tells you that?

Options:
A. Constance
B. Walter
C. Mei
D. Henry
context:
[1] (about=Diane, episodic, t4 @2025-03-17T19:12:00) Right then. Proposal: we maintain a formal complaint log, Walter to keep it. We send a written escalation to the owner if there are five incidents in a calendar month. Henry to draft the protocol. Anyone object? D
[2] (about=Walter, episodic, t6 @2025-03-24T18:47:00) Members: the structure mirrors what we used in 1998 at the firm for low-level disputes. It worked then. I have one suggested amendment, will send by email.
agent_answer:
B. Walter.

Walter’s reaction signals less than full agreement: instead of simply accepting the proposal, he says he has “one suggested amendment” that he will send by email. That indicates he was not fully on board with the protocol as proposed.

query:
During the discussion of the resident permit scheme, the group landed on doing the permits without any block-naming campaign attached. What did Aisling's response in that exchange reveal about her actual position on the sign idea, and what specifically in how she responded tells you that?

Options:
A. Yara
B. Aisling
C. Sasha
D. Marek
context:
[1] (about=Aisling, episodic, t12 @2025-04-14T19:13:00) what if we framed it positively, 'a quieter, calmer Maple Hill'? could even tie it to the block sign idea i had, same campaign, same imagery, less resistance overall imo
[2] (about=Greg, episodic, t12 @2025-04-14T19:14:00) ais we are not doing the sign. drop it
agent_answer:
**B. Aisling**

Aisling’s response reveals that she actually still supported the block-sign / block-naming idea, even though the group ultimately went with permits only. She tried to keep the sign idea alive by proposing positive framing — *“a quieter, calmer Maple Hill”* — and suggested tying it to the sign idea:

> “could even tie it to the block sign idea i had, same campaign, same imagery, less resistance overall imo”

The phrase **“tie it to the block sign idea i had”** shows she was still attached to the sign concept and was pitching it as a way to reduce resistance. Greg then shut it down: *“ais we are not doing the sign. drop it.”* So her response shows she favored the sign campaign, but the group decided against it.

query:
The group decided to raise the community fund float threshold from 200 to 250 pounds. One member's reply to that decision conveyed something different from the rest. Whose response signalled a meaningful reservation, and what specifically in how they responded tells you that?

Options:
A. Henry
B. Owen
C. Walter
D. Diane
context:
[1] (about=Walter, episodic, t16 @2025-04-28T19:03:00) Members: I would observe that 250 pounds carrying balance is at the upper edge of comfortable. I have always favoured a tighter float. However, if the group's view is that 250 is needed for the coming quarter, I will not block it.
[2] (about=Diane, episodic, t16 @2025-04-28T19:26:00) Lovely. Item one carries unanimously. Item two: float threshold raised to 250. Walter has formally accepted. Henry, please update the spreadsheet. D
agent_answer:
C. Walter.

His response signalled a meaningful reservation: he called the 250-pound threshold “at the upper edge of comfortable,” said he has “always favoured a tighter float,” and only agreed because he “will not block it” if the group needs 250 for the coming quarter. That is reluctant acceptance rather than wholehearted support, even though Diane later described it as formal acceptance under a unanimous item.
